root_cause.text: The Rust Binder range allocator implemented oneway-spam detection incorrectly by checking TreeRange before inserting the current allocation and by not implementing equivalent low_oneway_space() checks for ArrayRange, so the active async transaction was omitted or never evaluated.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says “The spam detection logic in TreeRange was executed before the current request was inserted into the tree” and “the detection logic for ArrayRange was missing altogether”; the patch moves the TreeRange oneway_spam_detected calculation to after insertion in tree.rs and adds low_oneway_space() plus a returned detection flag in array.rs/mod.rs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend `reserve_new` to return an extra boolean status together with the reservation result.
intent_record.what: The function signature of `reserve_new` was changed so its return type is now `Result<(usize, bool)>` instead of `Result<usize>`, while the parameters and surrounding logic shown in the diff remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, successful calls to `reserve_new` can now return an additional boolean value alongside the `usize`, enabling callers to receive extra status information from the reservation operation rather than only the numeric result.

intent_record.intent_summary: Detect and report probable one-way transaction spam during buffer reservation when async space is running low.
intent_record.what: The function `reserve_new` was changed to compute a boolean `oneway_spam_detected` based on whether the reservation is one-way, whether remaining one-way space falls below `self.size / 10`, and the result of a new helper method `low_oneway_space(pid)`, and its return value was changed from `Ok(insert_at_offset)` to `Ok((insert_at_offset, oneway_spam_detected))`. A new method `low_oneway_space(&self, calling_pid: Pid) -> bool` was added, which iterates over `self.ranges`, sums the sizes and counts the number of one-way buffers owned by the given pid, and returns true if that pid has more than 50 such buffers or more than `self.size / 4` of total allocation size.
intent_record.how: At runtime, buffer reservation now reports whether a likely one-way spam condition has been detected for the calling pid. Detection is only evaluated for one-way allocations when remaining one-way space is low, and then flags callers that already hold many one-way buffers or a large share of one-way space. This enables the caller to identify and react to probable async transaction spam when buffer space becomes constrained.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate the actual oneway spam detection flag from array.reserve_new in the array-backed reserve_new path.
intent_record.what: In the Impl::Array branch of reserve_new, the result of array.reserve_new(...) was changed from a single offset value to a tuple destructuring of (offset, oneway_spam_detected), and the ReserveNewSuccess initializer now passes through the returned oneway_spam_detected value instead of hardcoding it to false.
intent_record.how: This makes reserve_new propagate the oneway spam detection status produced by the array allocator at runtime, so callers receive the actual detection result rather than always seeing false in the array-backed path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused oneway spam-detection check from `reserve_new` so allocation no longer performs that redundant low-space evaluation at this point.
intent_record.what: The change removes the local `oneway_spam_detected` boolean and its associated comment block from `reserve_new`, deleting the computation that checked `is_oneway`, compared `new_oneway_space` against `self.size / 10`, and called `self.low_oneway_space(pid)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates the oneway spam-detection check from this point in `reserve_new`, so the function no longer evaluates low async-space conditions or invokes `low_oneway_space(pid)` here before proceeding to buffer allocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Detect and report one-way transaction spam when async buffer space falls below a low-space threshold while avoiding unnecessary checks.
intent_record.what: A new local boolean variable `oneway_spam_detected` is introduced before returning from `reserve_new`, computed as `is_oneway && new_oneway_space < self.size / 10 && self.low_oneway_space(pid)`, along with comments explaining that spam detection begins when less than 20% of async space remains, and the returned tuple now includes this computed value.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now conditionally triggers one-way spam detection only for one-way transactions and only when remaining one-way space drops below one tenth of the total buffer size, relying on short-circuit evaluation to avoid calling `low_oneway_space(pid)` unless the threshold is crossed. This enables reporting suspected spam pressure when async buffer space becomes low.

This matches the root cause: incorrect detection timing and missing equivalent checks for ArrayRange causing the active async transaction to be omitted or not evaluated.

candidates.rationale: This is the core flawed check in the tree allocator: it performs one-way spam detection before the current allocation is inserted, so the active async transaction is omitted from evaluation.

This hardcodes the array-backed path to report no oneway spam detection at all, matching the root cause that ArrayRange lacked equivalent low-space/spam detection and never evaluated the current async allocation.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the flawed oneway-spam detection in the tree allocator. It evaluates low_oneway_space() before inserting the current allocation, so the active async transaction is not included in the spam-detection decision.

This hardcodes the array-backed allocation path to never report oneway spam detection, reflecting the missing equivalent low_oneway_space() handling for ArrayRange and causing async allocations there to never be evaluated.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is visible directly in `reserve_new()` and `low_oneway_space()`, so the snippet is sufficient. In `reserve_new()`, the code computes `oneway_spam_detected` before inserting/updating the current allocation into the tree: `let oneway_spam_detected = is_oneway && new_oneway_space < self.size / 10 && self.low_oneway_space(pid);` This happens before the later block where the chosen free descriptor is converted into an allocated/reserved oneway descriptor: `desc.state = Some((DescriptorState::new(is_oneway, debug_id, pid), desc_node_res)); desc.size = size;`. Therefore `self.low_oneway_space(pid)` scans only the pre-existing tree state and omits the active async transaction being allocated. The helper `low_oneway_space()` confirms this behavior because it iterates `for (_, desc) in self.tree.iter()` and counts only descriptors already present with `state.is_oneway()` and matching `pid()`. There is no logic to include the current pending allocation in that accounting. This matches the root cause that TreeRange checks happen before inserting the current allocation. There is also no visible fix that would re-check after insertion or explicitly include `size`/current transaction in the spam calculation. Hence the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it directly shows how oneway spam detection is handled for both allocator variants. In the `Impl::Array(array)` arm, after `array.reserve_new(args.debug_id, args.size, args.is_oneway, args.pid)?`, the function unconditionally returns `oneway_spam_detected: false` (lines 190-199). This matches the root cause that equivalent low_oneway_space()/oneway-spam detection was not implemented for the ArrayRange path, so async allocations in the array-backed allocator are never evaluated for spam detection. By contrast, in the `Impl::Tree(tree)` arm, the result of `tree.reserve_new(...)` includes `(offset, oneway_spam_detected)` and propagates that value (lines 213-218), showing detection exists only there. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet present because the Array path still hardcodes `false` instead of performing proper detection.
